Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "can you check if we can manage project requirements (as the rest of the documents, both as documentation, but also both as ability to insert the requirements brief in the sessions and contextually where applicable, with the respective check in the agent sessions, the same as managing rules, policies, goals, exposing requirements to the user to manage with all the abilities to edit, delete, list, duplication checks, etc) - as for example to manage requirements of how the software to build - aka use cmake, conan, this type of format of cmake, etc. Such requirements and standards should be possible to be checked and received both from external tools (codeguide-mcp or other mcp servers), corporate policies (remote, local), or per project requirements, user managed imposed, or stored as requirements doc files, managed by ddflow. Check if we have these features, or we plan to implement them, what of the internal cores we could reuse, how to make the rules, requirements, goal, policies, documentation, skills, subagents, etc - to be instructing periodically the agent sessions, are we having gaps, how to improve on that. Do a deep research, and propose phase + tasks for corrections if any"

Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/requirements-management.md (task RQM-research) and the research notes R-req-* recorded 2026-10-21.

WHAT THIS PHASE IS: ENGINEERING requirements and standards (how the software is built: CMake >= 3.25, Conan 2 for dependencies, CMakePresets, no in-source builds, compiler flags, language style, licensing, security, branching/PR, test and documentation policy), as one scoped, layered, verifiable record that reaches agents contextually and periodically and leaves compliance evidence. It is NOT the product-requirements pipeline of P-product-docs (EARS text, stakeholders, baselines, RFP packs); both use the SAME shipped record kind, ddflow/templates/kinds/requirement.toml, which already exists (lifecycle proposed..verified, source, stakeholders) but is inert: no scoping, no strength, no verification, no injection (RecordKind.applies is declared and unused, api/records.py; guidance inject.collect returns rules and decisions only, services/guidance/inject.py:104). RQM-model extends the descriptor with a `class` field (product | constraint | standard | policy); PD-req-kind adds its EARS/baseline fields on top of the same descriptor. Do not build a second engine.

REUSE (confirmed in code): record surface (CRUD, search, recall, resources, history, supersede, merge, split: B-rc-lifecycle/participation done); data kinds (SE-kind-data done); guidance engine scoping, ranking, budget, provenance fence, similarity dedupe (services/guidance); checks and waivers modules (built, tested, UNWIRED: no caller outside services/guidance); doc types and B-dt-rules guidance-per-document; the cadenced footer (config_sections/reinstruct.py, services/obligations.py); agent brief (services/agent_brief.py); companions registry; org layers (P-org-config) for corporate sources.

SEQUENCING: the first tasks depend only on done work. Doors that need the open record-contract tasks (RQM-doors needs B-rc-context and B-rc-changes), org layers (RQM-layers needs B-org-layers, B-org-sources, B-org-trust), the pipeline field (RQM-gate needs B-pipe-model) and the strength/override model (RQM-strength needs B-goal-deviation) are explicitly gated on them; nothing here re-implements those. Held behind the P-gaps core/docs wave like P-goals per D-old-work-behind-core-docs unless the operator lifts it.

data.body:
Ask the operator and file the decision document. Recommended defaults (research section 'Recommended design'): (1) ONE kind `requirement` (the shipped template) with `class` = product|constraint|standard|policy, not a second 'standard' kind; P-product-docs adds EARS/baseline fields to the same descriptor. (2) strength = MUST (block, waive|none) / SHOULD (warn, deviate) / MAY (advisory) reusing the P-goals mapping (D-goals-principles). (3) layers org > team > project > local > task; a lower layer may only TIGHTEN (raise strength, narrow scope, add a verify) unless a person records a scoped, reasoned, expiring waiver. (4) injection tiers: always-on charter capped at [requirements].charter_tokens (default 250), contextual by glob/context at claim and pre-edit, on-demand search, periodic digest at a cadence; compaction re-sends the charter. (5) an agent may PROPOSE a requirement and accept only the low-risk classes the knob names (D-product-docs-r3 pattern); a person accepts the rest. (6) remote sources are trust=imported, pinned by digest, never auto-applied above SHOULD without a person's approval. (7) no `[policy]` duplicate: org enforced floor is B-org-policy. Write docs/ddflow/decisions/requirements.md and record decisions with --globs.

`ddflow requirement for [PATH...|--item ID]` prints the effective set, ranked, with the reason each applies (glob, context, gate, always), like clang-tidy --dump-config. Contexts are data: a context is a name plus file matchers (cmake: CMakeLists.txt, *.cmake, CMakePresets.json; conan: conanfile.py, conanfile.txt, conan.lock; cpp: *.cpp,*.hpp,*.h,*.cc) in a shipped contexts table, overridable per project; reuse the stack probe (SC-probe) when present, never a second scan. The match reads the item's declared globs AND the actual diff (changed_paths), like pipeline requirements (D-pipeline-requirements). Reuse services/guidance/resolve.py scope semantics. Acceptance: a task touching CMakeLists.txt gets the CMake requirements and not the Python ones; a task touching only docs gets neither.

data.body:
Tier 0 charter: one line per MUST requirement (id, 12 words, strength) capped at [requirements].charter_tokens (default 250) in the SessionStart brief and the MCP initialize block, never trimmed (pinned like inject.pinned). Tier 1 contextual: full statement + verify command for requirements matching the item/globs at claim (api/lifecycle/claim.py), in gate prompts (api/gates.py) and in review prompts with the verify-and-cite-id instruction (inject.VERIFY). Tier 2 on demand: `ddflow_recall`/`requirement for` search. Measured on this repo (research doc): SessionStart payload 5,374 B (~1,343 tok), brief 4,208 B, claim guidance block ~304 tok (door budget = 25% of session.brief_max_tokens=1200), agent launch brief 8,787 B (cap 9000), MCP initialize instructions 12,718 chars (~3.2k tok, pointers only, no rule text). The charter must fit inside the existing budget: it REPLACES the unreadable 'N more cut' line, it is not added on top. Acceptance: byte/token caps tested; a MUST requirement is never cut for a SHOULD; dropped ids are listed as '+N more: ddflow requirement for'.

data.body:
services/guidance/checks.py (run_record, gate_verdict) and waivers.py are built and tested but have no caller and no registered check kind (confirmed by grep). Register requirement check kinds: `command` (argv + expected exit, run through services/cmdrunner.py, timeout, cwd the worktree; e.g. `cmake --version` >= 3.25 via a small version-compare checker), `pattern` (regex present/absent in globbed files: no `-O3` in CMakeLists.txt, no in-source build marker), `file` (CMakePresets.json exists, conan.lock committed), `config` (key assertion in toml/json: cmake_minimum_required VERSION), `reviewer` (NL, evaluated through the standards/reviewer pool, RQM-reviewer), `mcp` (RQM-mcp-client). Result = passed|failed|unavailable|waived|inconclusive with the evidence (command, exit, output excerpt, digest of requirement and of the checked files); a check that could not run is `unavailable`, never passed. Emits `requirement.checked`. `ddflow requirement check [--item ID|PATH...|--all] [--json]` exits 0/1/2. Untrusted command rule: a verify command written by an agent or imported is inert until approved by digest (B-gap-command-trust). Acceptance: the CMake example fails on a seeded bad CMakeLists.txt and passes on the fixed one; an unrunnable checker is `unavailable`.

data.title: Requirement documents managed by ddflow: docs/requirements/*.md front matter <-> records, a generated REQUIREMENTS.md doc type and export

data.body:
Register `requirement` as a syncable kind in the org layer stack (B-org-kinds) instead of a separate loader: the org-defaults and org-ENFORCED layers (D-config-layer-order; enforced wins and a project may tighten, never loosen) carry requirement records read-only in the project (B-rc-lifecycle-guard read-only org sources). Resolution function `effective(layers) -> records` with per-record origin (layer, source uri, rev, digest) shown by `requirement show`; a lower layer replaces by id only to tighten (strength up, scope narrower, verify added); a loosening attempt is reported as a conflict (RQM-conflicts) and ignored. Local machine-level file layer (user-wide standards) is the same mechanism with a local source. Acceptance: org MUST cannot be demoted by a project record; a project may add a SHOULD and tighten; provenance asserted in tests.

data.title: Layered requirement sources and precedence: org > team > project > local > task, tighten-only, provenance on every record

data.body:
Config `[[requirements.source]]` (id, type = file|url|git|mcp, uri, layer, ref, pin = digest, refresh, mode = propose|apply). Reuse the org source fetchers and lock file (B-org-sources/B-org-lock) for url and git; add no second fetcher. Behaviour from OPA bundles: conditional GET (ETag/If-None-Match), verify before activation, keep the last good version on failure, offline mode uses the lock; pinned digest mismatch is refused and shown; records arrive as trust=imported (core/provenance), fenced as DATA, and a source of unknown trust may only PROPOSE (a person accepts) never apply a MUST.
